html:
The Laos to China railway runs about 420 km from Vientiane, the capital of Laos, north to Boten on the Chinese border. It opened in December 2021 and links straight into the Chinese network toward Kunming.

Before it Laos, a landlocked and mountainous country, had only a few kilometres of track across the Friendship Bridge from Thailand. The new line needed many tunnels and bridges, and cut a long road journey to a few hours. Fast trains carry passengers, and freight trains carry fruit, rubber and minerals north and Chinese goods south.

It was built and is mostly owned by Chinese state companies, as one of the showcase projects of China's Belt and Road Initiative. Laos borrowed heavily for its share, and its debts to China have raised worries about how a poor country can pay for such a project.

The plan is to join the line across the Mekong to a Thai high-speed railway, so that trains could run from China through Laos to Bangkok and on toward Malaysia and Singapore.
